title: DFA: RORE Deal With China 'Never Restricted' Philippine Rights
detail: The Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs on August 13, 2026 issued a further clarification of the Provisional Understanding on Rotation and Resupply (RORE) missions to BRP Sierra Madre at Ayungin Shoal, again responding to criticism from retired Justice Antonio Carpio. The DFA said the arrangement 'was crafted expressly without prejudice to the Arbitral Award' and covers only personnel rotation and material resupply principles, without limiting Philippine sovereignty under the 2016 Arbitral Award. The department called Carpio's concerns 'misplaced,' noting alternative resupply methods such as airdrops, drones and fast boats had been studied before the provisional understanding was adopted, and invited Carpio to raise his proposals directly with the AFP and Philippine Coast Guard for an operational feasibility assessment.

media.caption: DFA headquarters; the department says the RORE arrangement never restricted Philippine rights

title: Teodoro Accuses China of 'Extortion and Blackmail' After Beijing 'Takes Action' Against 100+ Filipinos
detail: Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. on August 13, 2026 accused China of 'plain and simple extortion and blackmail' after Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun confirmed on August 10 that Chinese immigration authorities had 'taken action' against more than 100 Filipino nationals for illegal employment and illegal residence in China. Teodoro said the move was retaliatory for the Philippines' May 15 raid on Sanjia Steel Corp. in Tagoloan, Misamis Oriental, which arrested roughly 69-70 Chinese nationals — later released after consular intervention — on suspected immigration, labor-safety and radioactive-materials violations. 'We strongly condemn both the attempt by China to interfere in our law enforcement processes and the blatant blackmail against Filipinos,' Teodoro said, arguing the detained Chinese nationals were principals of illegal enterprises operating under a court-issued search warrant, not rank-and-file workers.

media.caption: Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. accused China of extortion and blackmail over its crackdown on Filipino nationals
